title: One Earth Building Held Up to 800 People — Fujian Tulou | China Travel Expert
description:
Imagine an apartment block built entirely out of packed earth — and a single one could hold up to 800 people.

These are tulou, the giant communal earth buildings of China's Hakka communities in Fujian. Thick rammed-earth walls, often several storeys high, wrap around a central courtyard. For defense there is usually just one door in, and windows only above the ground floor. One tulou could house an entire clan — up to 800 residents — with homes, wells and storerooms all inside the ring. In 2008, 46 of them were inscribed as the Fujian Tulou UNESCO World Heritage Site.

🧭 Expert Tip: step into the courtyard and look up — the stacked wooden galleries show how dozens of families shared one wall; a few tulou still have residents today.

一座土楼，夯土厚墙、往往只有一个大门，能住下整个家族近800人——2008年，46座福建土楼列入世界遗产。
